key_idea: Either the subarray lies in one row (an arithmetic progression with difference i dividing a_1, giving k = max(i, a_n/i)), or it crosses a row end at some j, where a_{j+1} = i+1 and a_j = i*k pin down both the row and k.
sketch: Try the no-break candidate: all differences equal d>0 with d | a_1, k = max(d, a_n/d). Then for each j treat it as a row boundary: i = a_{j+1}-1, k = a_j/i must be an integer with k >= i+1, the start index (i-1)k+(k-1)-j must be non-negative and the window must fit in k*k cells; verify all n cells in O(n). Answer is the minimum valid k; O(n^2) per test. Later breaks need no special handling since the verification simulates the flat index. Checked against a brute force over small tables.
